question: If one AI tool helps us work for hours and another reminds us to rest, which do we need more?
reflection: Tools that know when to step back can help people stay healthy and thoughtful while they get more done.

sources.subject: ChatGPT Work Agent, Claude Reflect Dashboard, SWE-1.7 at $1.97/task

one_line: OpenAI launched an agent mode that carries out whole work projects for hours, while Anthropic added a dashboard that shows how people use Claude and nudges them to take breaks.

top_stories.title: ChatGPT Work runs whole projects
top_stories.what: OpenAI launched ChatGPT Work, a mode built on GPT-5.6 that takes a goal, pulls data from connected apps such as Drive and Slack, works for hours and returns finished documents, slides, sheets or simple web apps.
top_stories.why: Agents that produce full deliverables change what clients will expect from analysts and consultants, and how fast.

top_stories.title: Claude shows users their own habits
top_stories.what: Anthropic added Reflect, a dashboard showing when and how much a person uses Claude, the topics they raise most, plus quiet hours and break reminders.
top_stories.why: Built-in nudges to rest are a clear behavioural design choice worth studying for digital well-being.

top_stories.title: A cheaper coding model from Cognition
top_stories.what: Cognition released SWE-1.7, built on an open Kimi model and trained further with reinforcement learning; it reports near-top coding scores at about two dollars per task.
top_stories.why: Strong results from a tuned open base model show that the top labs are not the only route to high quality.

top_stories.title: Cohere releases a multilingual vision model
top_stories.what: Cohere Labs released Aya Vision, an 8B open-weight model that reads images and supports 23 languages.
top_stories.why: Open multilingual models are a useful starting point for testing image and document tasks outside English.

saudi_lens.text: Healthy-use features matter in Saudi Arabia, where young people are heavy digital users; usage dashboards could inform national digital well-being campaigns.

idea.title: Digital well-being nudge study
idea.pitch: Test whether break reminders and usage summaries change how long people spend with AI assistants at work and how they feel about it.
idea.first_step: Design a two-week diary study with a small volunteer group, half with reminders turned on.

idea_kids.title: My screen time diary
idea_kids.pitch: A paper diary where children colour in the time they spend on screens, outdoors and with family each day, then talk about the balance at the end of the week.
idea_kids.first_step: Design a one-page weekly chart with three colours and a small reflection box.

terms.definition: An AI system that can plan and carry out several steps on its own to reach a goal.
What it costs in AI usage fees to complete one piece of work, a fairer measure than price per word.
Relying on an AI tool for comfort or company to a degree that may crowd out human support.

concepts.summary: Agent modes that deliver finished documents and apps from a single goal.
Usage dashboards and break nudges as a design for healthier AI use.
Coding models tuned from open bases reach near-top scores at low cost.
